newsitem.title: USA: Rexene sees flat to higher Q2 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Rexene sees flat to higher Q2 EPS.

text.p: Rexene Corp said Tuesday it expects second-quarter earnings per share to match or exceed the year-earlier $0.39 if the present trend of lower feedstock prices continues.
In the first quarter, higher feedstock costs cut operating earnings by about $0.39 a share, the company said.

"Feedstock prices have declined from the unusually high levels experienced at the beginning of the year and appear to be moving in ranges similar to last year's second and third quarters," said Chairman Andrew Smith.

"At the same time, we continue to see strong demand and price stability in our polyethylene, polypropylene and styrene businesses, as well as increased volumes and steady prices in our CT Film business.
"We also are benefiting from growing contributions from our new REXflex FPO plant, which began production in December 1996, and the continued growth of our REXtac APAO business," he said.
"If these trends continue, we expect second quarter earnings to meet or exceed the $0.39 per share reported in the second quarter of 1996."

Significantly higher feedstock costs in late 1996 and early 1997 reduced Rexene's operating earnings for the first quarter by about $7.5 million after tax, or $0.39 per share, compared to the same period in 1996.

Earnings per share for the first quarter were reduced by $0.04 per share due to costs associated with ongoing proxy solicitation expenses. The company also recorded a severance charge of $320,000, or $0.01 per share, for labor reductions that will result in annual cost savings for the CT Film Division of about $2 million.
